home.amuni_text:
Amunì, in the Sicilian dialect, means 'let's go'. It is a warm invitation to move, to explore, and to let yourself be guided among our thousand-year-old stones, keepers of tales, noblewomen and ancient prayers.

Don't stop your steps, look at yourself in this magic: Amunì, come, I'll show you the way.

transport_page.welcome: Welcome, traveler, to the Transport section. Here you will find the information you need to get around near the village.
transport_page.company_desc: The bus line connects Caccamo to Termini Imerese and Palermo all year round. Taking the morning and afternoon runs (the 9am and 1pm departures) towards Palermo, you can get off at Vetrana, a well-known seaside spot, at Pietra Piatta, or at the 'Venus's navel' rock formation. From Termini Imerese you can also catch a train to Cefalù and other tourist destinations.
transport_page.stop_1: Porta Euracea: opposite the Bar Giallombardo and the building materials shop.
transport_page.stop_2: Viale Regione Siciliana: above the 'Roberta' playground (near the Axa insurance agency).
transport_page.stop_3: Piazza Cappuccini: in the shade of the old Convent.

castello.title: The Castle of Caccamo
castello.description: The Castle has stood on this cliff since 1094, built by the Normans to dominate the San Leonardo valley. In 1160 it was the setting for the barons' conspiracy: the lord Matteo Bonello took refuge here after attempting to overthrow King William I. It is said that his ghost still wanders the Hall of the Conspiracy, in search of peace. One of the chapels even hides a trapdoor, once used to get rid of unwelcome guests.
castello.hours: Winter hours (16 October - 14 April): Monday afternoon - Sunday, 09:00 – 12:30 and 14:30 – 18:30. Summer hours (15 April - 15 October): Monday afternoon - Sunday, 09:00 – 12:30 and 15:30 – 19:00. Closed Monday morning.
castello.tickets: Full price € 6.00 | Promotional with online booking € 4.50 | Residents of the Municipality of Caccamo € 1.00 | Students aged 18-25 € 3.00 | Free under 18. Info and bookings: 091 8103233 (Mon-Fri) or 091 8149252 (Tue-Sun).

badia.title: Church of San Benedetto alla Badia
badia.description: Behind its sober façade, the church houses one of the most precious majolica floors in Sicily: 5,555 hand-painted tiles from the 18th century, with a sailing ship battling a stormy sea at its center — a symbol of the Church against the forces of evil. Locals still call it the 'parlour church' for its wealth of stucco work and gilded inlays. Many visitors choose to walk through it barefoot, out of respect and to appreciate every detail.
badia.tickets: Full price € 2.00 | Reduced € 1.00 (EU youth aged 18-25 or with a same-day Castle ticket) | Free under 18

santamaria.title: Church of Santa Maria degli Angeli
santamaria.description: The people of Caccamo still call it 'San Domenico', after the name of the square. It was founded in 1487 by the Dominican friar Giovanni Liccio, born right here in Caccamo — according to tradition, the Madonna herself showed him in a dream where to build it. Today the church holds his relics in a silver urn, alongside a Madonna and Child carved in 1516 by Antonello Gagini. It is the same Blessed Giovanni whom the village celebrates every May.
santamaria.hours: Summer hours 2026 (from 5 July): Weekdays 08:30. Sundays and holidays 08:30 and 18:00.
santamaria.rettore: The church is cared for by Father Nicasio Galbo, a spiritual point of reference for the village, always ready to welcome with open arms anyone who visits.
santamaria.restauro_vetrate: In recent years the church has undergone major restoration work, including the beautiful stained-glass windows: looking up from the central nave you can admire them above the entrance, and equally striking are those in the dome above the altar.
santamaria.statua_beato: The statue of Blessed Giovanni Liccio — the "purest white lily, son of Caccamo" — has recently been moved to a more accessible spot for visitors.
santamaria.bassorilievo: Continuing towards the sacristy you'll find a bas-relief of the Madonna, also restored: it tells a story from local devotion, of the Madonna throwing an anchor to a wealthy grain merchant sailing to Termini Imerese, saving him from a shipwreck.
santamaria.beato_giovanni_mondo: Devotion to Blessed Giovanni Liccio is also strong in Chicago, home to a large community of devotees. In Caccamo, a grotto dedicated to him is a site of pilgrimage for the local community, currently suspended for safety works in the area.
santamaria.beato_giovanni_link_label: 🔗 Learn more about Blessed Giovanni Liccio

sangiorgio.title: Church of San Giorgio Martire
sangiorgio.description: The Cathedral stands where, according to tradition, the Normans built the first church dedicated to San Giorgio as early as 1090 — the saint said to have helped them defeat the Saracens at the Battle of Cerami in 1063. The building you see today dates back to the 17th century, but its 49-metre-tall bell tower is even older: its lower part was once a watchtower for the Castle. Inside, the baroque altar houses reliefs attributed to Francesco Laurana and a silver reliquary statue of Santa Rosalia.
sangiorgio.hours: Summer service hours: 11:00 – 18:30. Winter service hours: 11:00 – 18:00.
sangiorgio.secret_info: 💒 Sunday Masses in Caccamo: on Sunday mornings, Mass is also celebrated in two smaller churches, open only for this occasion. The Chiesa del Carmine (9:00 am) is located in a peripheral area of the village, reached by following Via del Carmine towards the barracks and then climbing up to the small square where the church stands. The Chiesa di San Giovanni li Greci (10:00 am) lies instead in a rural hamlet of Caccamo, reachable only by car. Two evocative stops for anyone wanting to experience local faith at its most authentic, off the usual paths.

sangiorgio_gallery.dettagliocappellare: Detail of the Chapel of the Relics

annunziata.title: Parish of SS. Annunziata
annunziata.description: Its origins date back to the 13th century, making it one of the oldest in Caccamo. It houses a large canvas by Guglielmo Borremans, the Annunciation, and stucco work from the school of Serpotta. In the 18th century it also had a majolica floor painted by the master Nicolò Sarzana — the same craftsman who later created the famous floor of the nearby Badia church. Every spring, the church comes alive for the feast of San Giuseppe, one of the most cherished traditions in the village.
annunziata.hours: Summer weekday hours: Holy Mass at 18:00 (in August at 19:00). Sundays and holidays: Holy Masses at 09:30, 12:00 and 19:00.
annunziata.fiera_agosto_title: Celebrations in honour of Saint Nicasius the Martyr
annunziata.fiera_agosto_description: From 23 to 30 August, Solemn Octave: Rosary at 18:00, Little Crown at 18:30, Holy Mass at 19:00. Sunday 30 August: a day of celebration with the Dawn Ringing and Solemn Vespers. Monday 31 August: Solemnity of Saint Nicasius the Martyr, patron saint of Caccamo — Solemn Mass with Panegyric (11:00), Mass with Civil and Military Authorities (18:00), Solemn procession with fireworks display (19:30). Sunday 13 September: Return of the relic to its shrine.

cappuccini.title: Convent of the Capuchin Friars
cappuccini.description: The Capuchin friars arrived here in 1589, bringing with them the sober, quiet style that has always distinguished their order. It is one of the last still-inhabited convents in all of western Sicily: today, as then, the friars live by prayer, manual work and the welcoming of pilgrims. Its walls tell almost two centuries of history, even before the Unification of Italy.
cappuccini.hours: Accessible mainly before or after services. Open daily from 16:00 to 20:00.
cappuccini.secret_info: 💡 The Hidden Gems of Caccamo: The village is home to as many as 33 churches. Use the Din Don Dan map and zoom in on Caccamo to discover real-time hours and openings of lesser-known treasures and other small hidden masterpieces. From 1 to 15 August, the convent will hold the "quindicina", a fifteen-day novena in honour of Our Lady of the Assumption. Holy Rosary at 18:00, Coroncina at 18:30, Holy Mass at 19:00.

animesante.title: Church of the Holy Souls of Purgatory
animesante.description: The Church of the Holy Souls of Purgatory is one of the village's hidden gems. Here you'll find Serpotta stuccoes, paintings by Giovanni Bonomo, the catacombs, and even an ancient colatoio where the first stage of the embalming process once took place. The church is made accessible thanks to the Confraternity of the Holy Souls of Purgatory, which not only provides expert guides on Sundays but also organises events to promote the area.
animesante.confraternita_text: The Confraternity of the Holy Souls in Purgatory dedicates time and resources to this church: we deeply appreciate their volunteer work and their resilience. The partnership between the confraternity and the Vivere è Pensare association is designed to host events on site within the monument, letting visitors fully appreciate its beauty from every angle.
animesante.address: Piazza Duomo, next to the Monte di Pietà
animesante.event_date: Saturday 16 August – 6:30 PM – Under the Stars of the Confraternity
animesante.event_text: An evening organised by the Confraternity of the Holy Souls of Purgatory, open to the whole community of Caccamo, held both outside and inside the church. It opens with a concert by Renato Filippello and a violinist, followed by an activity for children and a rosary under the stars. The evening closes with a shared moment of bread, olive oil and wine. Expected duration: about two to two and a half hours.

vivereepensare_page.title: "Vivere è Pensare" Cultural Association
vivereepensare_page.welcome: A reference point for anyone who loves Caccamo and wants to experience it through art, music and community.
vivereepensare_page.desc: Founded in Caccamo, the association promotes culture, art, music and solidarity in the village, often working alongside the Municipality of Caccamo, FIDAPA Caccamo chapter, the "Amici della Musica B. Albanese" Association and the Pro Loco.
vivereepensare_page.activity_1: Art exhibitions, such as painting shows in the Church of Sant'Antonio Abate
vivereepensare_page.activity_2: Musical evenings: jazz, clarinet quartets and sunset concerts
vivereepensare_page.activity_3: Cultural walks discovering the neighbourhoods, churches and lesser-known secrets of Caccamo
vivereepensare_page.activity_4: "Sensi in Corte", a multisensory experience with tastings, art and music
vivereepensare_page.activity_5: The "Vivere è Pensare" Award - Che cielo, che stelle!, which every year celebrates stories, people and realities from the local area
vivereepensare_page.closing: Follow them to discover upcoming events!
vivereepensare_page.event1_text: Professor Battistella recites verses from the Purgatorio of Dante's Divine Comedy, inside the Church of the Holy Souls of Purgatory. An hour of reading and poetry, organised by the Vivere è Pensare Association with the collaboration of GeA and the Confraternity of the Holy Souls of Purgatory, under the patronage of the Municipality of Caccamo. The Mayor and other institutional representatives will attend. Free admission. Violinist Giada Calderone will also perform during the evening. The event poster can be found on the organisers' social media pages.
vivereepensare_page.event2_date: 🕯️ Saturday 16 August – 6:30 PM – Under the Stars of the Confraternity
vivereepensare_page.event2_text: An evening organised by the Confraternity of the Holy Souls of Purgatory, open to the whole Caccamo community, in front of and inside the church. It opens with a concert by Renato Filippello and violinist Giada Calderone, followed by a moment dedicated to children and a rosary under the stars. The evening closes with a shared moment of bread, oil and wine. Expected duration: about two to two and a half hours. The event poster can be found on the organisers' social media pages.

events_page.title: Rites and Feasts of the Village
events_page.intro: Experience the most authentic soul of our village through its centuries-old traditions, where faith, history and folklore intertwine in unique and moving moments.
events_page.signuruzzu_desc: On Palm Sunday, a local child plays the role of Jesus and rides through the village streets, decked out for the feast with palm fronds, on a decorated donkey. The procession stops in front of the Church of Santa Maria degli Angeli and the Cathedral of San Giorgio Martire for a moving blessing.
events_page.venerdi_desc: The atmosphere grows solemn with the altars set up in the churches for Good Friday, adorned with the typical dishes of wheat sprouted in the dark. These are followed by the solemn and moving Procession and the town's Way of the Cross.
events_page.giovanni_desc: A deeply felt occasion, lived by the whole community, which gathers around its Blessed in a climate of great devotion and popular warmth.
events_page.castellana_title: Election of the Castellana & Historic Parade
events_page.castellana_desc: The village plunges back into its glorious medieval past. Every year, in the second half of August, a magnificent historic parade in period costume winds through the streets of the town. Every two years, the parade culminates in the solemn election of the Castellana of the castle, for which candidacies open in February.
events_page.nicasio_title: Feast of San Nicasio and the Palio
events_page.nicasio_desc: Vibrant celebrations in honor of the Saint, enriched by the eagerly awaited and thrilling town Palio, which sparks excitement and rivalry among young and old alike.
events_page.sagra_desc: Every year, on the second Sunday of October, the scents of tradition fill the village. An unmissable food event to taste authentic local sausage amid songs, wine and conviviality.
events_page.facebook_group_note: A group curated by a local resident with all of Caccamo's events, always up to date.
events_page.estate_description: A whole summer of events promoted by the Municipality: opera, music, sport and traditions at the foot of the Castle.
